segments.note: Bookmap chart displayed.

segments.speech: So for this setup, we're going to see aggressive selling coming off a supply zone. This also relates to a key level. For this type of scenario,
segments.note: Slide titled 'Aggressive Sellers off Key Level' displayed.

segments.speech: I would need to see it at a supply zone, or demand zone, or a key level, or just an important reference point from the chart.
It cannot be at a random level or random zone. I prefer not to see that. I prefer to see it at a supply, demand, or resistance, support level.
So here we have a 15-minute supply zone, and it was formed two days prior at 4220.25.
As you can see here, we have some consolidation. We even got some consolidation from the overnight session. The market opens up, consolidates,
segments.note: Switches to thinkorswim /ES 15m chart showing supply zone.

segments.speech: and then drops down lower. This validates our 15-minute demand zone. The market rallies at the open directly into this 15-minute,
and we sell off about 30 points lower from the high, all the way down into the low.
Now, we're going to see a very strong rally at the open. We're going to see very aggressive market buying, and as long as they put pressure,
segments.note: Returns to slide 'Aggressive Sellers off Key Level'.

segments.speech: they continuously hit the offer at the open and they're putting pressure, putting pressure, buying, buying, buying directly at the open and thereafter,
it's usually a good opportunity to scalp long, and it would best to be if it was like above a resistance level or it was holding VWAP.
But most of the time, and I said this in one of the previous lessons, that usually, but not always, at aggressive offer trades directly at the open—
we see it right here, we see it right here, we see it rally, we see it holding VWAP, right? And as long as they continuously put pressure
segments.note: Switches to Bookmap replay showing green buying bubbles at open.

segments.speech: and hold on dips and more buying comes in, it's a very good opportunity to scalp the market long.
And in this case, let's just say you even got long above 4210, you would have been able to catch a 10-point rally into that supply zone.
So quick little scalps, not exposing yourself very long for the market.
I'm going to pull up the depth of market, and let's keep going through this.
segments.note: DOM ladder opened briefly on Bookmap.

segments.speech: So what we're going to see is after this very strong buying and the very aggressive at-offer trades, we're going to get that rally into a supply zone,
segments.note: Returns to slide 'Aggressive Sellers off Key Level'.

segments.speech: and there's no real strong or clear absorption or any trapped participants.
We've been going over so far about trapped, about absorption, heavy selling, strong buying, et cetera.

segments.speech: In this example, we essentially rally into supply. Yeah, the delta's positive at supply where we have the high, because keep in mind,
remember what I said earlier about the market will move up until the last buyer buys. So in this example, you know, we have tons of buying up here,
but the buying got shut down and sellers eventually stepped into the market. The market's going to move up until the last buyer buys,
or there's a lack of buying, which the market then will have to—the sellers or the producers are going to have to lower their prices.
Others can take advantage of it by shorting or selling to capitalize on another further downside move until the market finds an area
of acceptance, of fair value, where buyers and sellers essentially are like agreeing on price.
So we're going to see a rally into the supply zone. We're not going to see any real strong absorption or trapped participants on the tape.
segments.note: Returns to slide 'Aggressive Sellers off Key Level'.

segments.speech: However, what we are going to see is as we rally into the supply zone—and remember what I said, this is really only valid at a key level
or a supply/demand imbalance—where we're going to see a lot of trades hitting the bid and below the bid, meaning aggressive sellers are stepping in,
after we reject that key level, or after we reject the supply zone. And then I'm going to get into filling low volume nodes in the profile.
So I'm going to pull up Bookmap here. I'm going to pull up the depth of market, and I'm actually even going to pull up a 15-minute chart
segments.note: Switches to thinkorswim 15m chart.

segments.speech: where we have that supply zone. We get a rally up into that supply zone and we fell. This is a 15-minute candle, so from the low to the high
is 4220 to a low of about 4191. So about 30 points from low to high.

If you say yes to both of them, then you put that trade on. Because if we're getting short right here at 4218,

so we're really risking three points at this moment, or call it four points, to make potentially,
in this example, the targets for this trade. And a little tip is when there is a lack of trade at a specific level,
so I pull up the volume profile, and this RTH is a regular trading hours volume profile, meaning just the cash session from 9:30 Eastern to 4:00 p.m.

segments.speech: When you see a price or multiple prices—I'd rather see multiple prices of it—where there's a lack of trade,
so you see how there was no trades done here where I'm hovering my cursor over on the bid? There's zero volume done at 4211 and a quarter on the bid side,

segments.speech: and there's zero volume done at 4210 and a quarter. So see how there's zero bid volume down here? That's a lack of trade at that area, or there's just a lack of volume.
It's not bullish, it's not bearish, however those tend to get filled. Not always, those tend to gravitate where price is going to head next.
So if I'm short up here at the 4218s, where I did enter this market short,
this is also an example where you cannot hesitate. If you hesitate, you are going to skew your risk-to-reward if you think about it too much,
or you question your entry, or you are too concerned about losing. If you hesitate on an entry like this and you get short, let's just say, at 4216 or 4215,

So going back to Bookmap, now that we understand that, as soon as you see the aggressive selling step in, you cannot hesitate.

Market's going to sell off into that, and you sell, if you're short, into that weakness. Or if you want to call it strength, you could call it strength. But you want to sell when the market is coming in your favor like that with a fast-moving tape,

slides.title: Aggressive Sellers off Key Level
slides.text:
• CONTEXT & Execution: 15m supply formed 2 days prior at 4220.25.
• Strong rally at the open. Aggressive market buying with continuous pressure directly at open usually is a good opportunity to scalp long.
• Rallied into supply. No real strong/clear absorption or trapped participants.
• Large trades hitting bid and below bid after rejecting supply.
• Filling in the LVNs in the profile.
